Chapter Overview

Gunakan bab ini sebagai modul belajar siswa. Ikuti urutan kegiatan, klik kalimat listening untuk mendengar TTS, dan kerjakan kuis interaktif di akhir.

Welcome to the Chapter

Have you ever wondered why the internet signal becomes slow during bad weather?

Have you ever asked why waves become stronger in certain months?

Have you ever noticed that some videos appear again and again on your social media feed?

Have you ever wondered why goods on small islands can become more expensive when the boat schedule is delayed?

Dalam bab ini, kamu akan belajar menjelaskan proses secara runtut dalam Bahasa Inggris. Kamu tidak hanya menghafal teori, tetapi juga belajar membaca fenomena di sekitar pulau, memahami prosesnya, lalu menjelaskannya dengan bahasa yang jelas, ilmiah, dan mudah dipahami.

Big Questions

  1. How does satellite internet work on remote islands?
    Bagaimana internet satelit bekerja di pulau terpencil?
  2. Why does coastal erosion happen?
    Mengapa abrasi pantai terjadi?
  3. How do social media algorithms recommend videos?
    Bagaimana algoritma media sosial merekomendasikan video?
  4. How can transportation costs affect prices on islands?
    Bagaimana biaya transportasi memengaruhi harga barang di pulau?

Learning Objectives

  • Identify the social function of an explanation text.
  • Identify the structure: general statement, sequenced explanation, and closing.
  • Recognize and use passive voice in technical explanations.
  • Use chronological connectors to explain process stages.
  • Use technical terms related to nature, technology, economy, and social life.
  • Analyze cause-effect relationships in explanation texts.
  • Write and present a clear explanation text using an infographic or PowerPoint.

Initial Understanding

Amati tiga situasi berikut. Diskusikan secara berpasangan sebelum masuk ke konsep utama.

Situation 1: Internet on the Island

During bad weather, internet connection becomes unstable. Some students think it happens only because many people use the internet. Others think the weather also affects the signal.

  1. What may cause the connection to become unstable?
  2. What systems are involved?
  3. How can you explain it in English?

Situation 2: Prices at a Small Island Shop

A shop owner says rice, cooking oil, and eggs become more expensive when the boat from the mainland is delayed.

  1. Why can transportation affect prices?
  2. What happens when supply is limited?
  3. How can this process be explained step by step?

Situation 3: Videos on Social Media

A student watches one video about football. After that, more football videos appear on his feed.

  1. What information may be collected?
  2. How does the system choose videos?
  3. What positive and negative effects can this process have?

Concept Lab: What Is an Explanation Text?

Pahami konsep dasar teks eksplanasi sebelum menganalisis teks panjang.

Definition

An explanation text is a text that explains how or why something happens. It explains a process, phenomenon, system, or event in a logical and scientific way.

Artinya: Teks eksplanasi adalah teks yang menjelaskan bagaimana atau mengapa sesuatu terjadi. Teks ini menjelaskan proses, fenomena, sistem, atau peristiwa secara runtut dan ilmiah.

Social Function

To explain the process of how something happens or why something happens.

Artinya: Menjelaskan proses bagaimana sesuatu terjadi atau mengapa sesuatu terjadi.

Common Topics

Topic AreaExamples
Natural Phenomenahow rain forms, how coastal erosion happens, how tidal floods occur
Technologyhow satellite internet works, how solar panels produce electricity
Social Phenomenahow information spreads online, how online habits are formed
Economyhow inflation happens, how transportation cost affects prices
Environmenthow plastic waste reaches the sea, how global warming occurs

Explanation Text vs Procedure Text vs Report Text

AspectExplanation TextProcedure TextReport Text
PurposeTo explain how or why something happensTo tell how to do or make somethingTo describe general facts about something
Main QuestionHow does it happen? Why does it happen?How do we do it?What is it like?
StructureGeneral statement, sequenced explanation, closingGoal, materials, stepsGeneral classification, description
Language FeaturesPassive voice, connectors, technical terms, cause-effectImperatives, action verbs, sequence wordsSimple present, descriptive language
Example TopicHow coastal erosion happensHow to make a water filterSeaweed as a marine plant

Text Structure of Explanation Text

1. General Statement

Introduces the phenomenon or process.

Guiding question: What is being explained?

2. Sequenced Explanation

Explains the stages of the process using connectors and cause-effect language.

Guiding question: How does it happen?

3. Closing Statement

Summarizes the impact or importance.

Guiding question: Why is it important?

Simple Example

Title: How Rainwater Is Collected on Small Islands

General Statement: Rainwater harvesting is a process of collecting and storing rainwater for daily needs.
Artinya: Pemanenan air hujan adalah proses mengumpulkan dan menyimpan air hujan untuk kebutuhan sehari-hari.

Sequenced Explanation: Initially, rainwater falls on the roof. Then, the water is directed through pipes. Following this, the water is stored in tanks or containers.
Artinya: Pada awalnya, air hujan jatuh di atap. Kemudian, air dialirkan melalui pipa. Setelah tahap ini, air disimpan di tandon atau wadah.

Closing: As a result, families can use the stored water when fresh water is limited.
Artinya: Sebagai hasilnya, keluarga dapat menggunakan air yang tersimpan ketika air tawar terbatas.

Language Focus

Bagian ini membahas passive voice, chronological connectors, cause-effect language, dan technical terms.

Language Focus 1: Passive Voice

Passive voice sering digunakan dalam penjelasan teknis karena fokusnya ada pada proses, benda, atau hasil, bukan selalu pada pelaku tindakan.

Present Passive

Subject + am/is/are + past participle

Rainwater is collected in tanks.
Air hujan dikumpulkan di tandon.

Past Passive

Subject + was/were + past participle

The coastline was damaged by strong waves.
Garis pantai rusak akibat ombak kuat.

Modal Passive

Subject + can be / must be / should be + past participle

The water should be filtered before use.
Air sebaiknya disaring sebelum digunakan.

Active and Passive Comparison

Active SentencePassive SentenceArti Bahasa IndonesiaFunction
People collect rainwater in tanks.Rainwater is collected in tanks.Air hujan dikumpulkan di tandon.Focus on water
The system recommends videos.Videos are recommended by the system.Video direkomendasikan oleh sistem.Focus on videos
Strong waves erode the coastline.The coastline is eroded by strong waves.Garis pantai terkikis oleh ombak kuat.Focus on coastline
Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity.Sunlight is converted into electricity by solar panels.Cahaya matahari diubah menjadi listrik oleh panel surya.Focus on sunlight
Boats deliver goods to the island.Goods are delivered to the island by boats.Barang dikirim ke pulau dengan kapal.Focus on goods
The platform records user behavior.User behavior is recorded by the platform.Perilaku pengguna dicatat oleh platform.Focus on user behavior

Connector Practice

  1. ________, rainwater falls on the roof.
    A. Finally B. Initially C. As a result D. Therefore E. Eventually
  2. The data is collected by the platform. ________, it is analyzed by the algorithm.
    A. Following this B. At first C. Finally D. Therefore E. As a result

    A. Initially B. First C. As a result D. Next E. Meanwhile

Reading Section

Baca tiga teks panjang berikut. Perhatikan struktur, passive voice, connectors, technical terms, dan cause-effect relationships.

Reading 1: How Coastal Erosion Happens on Small Islands

Coastal erosion is a natural process in which land near the sea is gradually worn away by waves, currents, tides, and wind. On small islands, this process can be more visible because the land area is limited and many people live close to the coastline. Coastal erosion does not usually happen in one day. It happens slowly through repeated natural forces, although human activities can make the process faster.

Initially, waves move toward the shore and hit the coastline. When the waves are strong, a large amount of energy is carried by the water. This energy pushes against sand, soil, rocks, or coral fragments along the beach. If the beach is not protected by natural barriers such as mangroves, coral reefs, or healthy vegetation, the force of the waves can reach the land more directly.

Following this, small particles of sand and soil are loosened. These particles are then carried away by waves and currents. This stage may not be noticed immediately because the amount of sand moved in one wave can be small. However, when the same process happens repeatedly, the shape of the beach begins to change. The shoreline may move closer to houses, roads, or public facilities.

Subsequently, tides can make the process more serious. During high tide, seawater reaches higher parts of the beach. If high tide happens together with strong wind or stormy weather, more water can enter low areas. As a result, the land may become softer and easier to erode. In some places, tidal floods can also occur when seawater flows into settlement areas during very high tides.

Coastal erosion can also be affected by human activities. For example, when coastal vegetation is removed, the soil loses natural protection. When sand or coral is taken from the beach, the coastline becomes weaker. In addition, climate change and sea level rise can increase the risk of erosion in coastal areas. Higher sea levels allow waves to reach farther inland, especially during extreme weather.

Finally, the effects of coastal erosion can be seen in daily life. Beaches may become narrower, coconut trees may fall, paths may be damaged, and houses near the sea may become more vulnerable. For island communities, understanding coastal erosion is important because it helps people plan safer settlements, protect vegetation, and reduce activities that damage the coast.

In conclusion, coastal erosion happens through a sequence of natural processes. Waves hit the shore, sand and soil are moved, tides bring seawater farther inland, and the coastline slowly changes. This process is natural, but it can be made worse when coastal environments are not protected.

Reading 2: How Social Media Algorithms Recommend Videos

A social media algorithm is a system that selects and recommends content based on user behavior. When people open a digital platform, they do not see random content only. Many posts, videos, and advertisements are chosen by the system because the platform tries to predict what users may watch, like, comment on, or share.

Initially, user activity is collected by the platform. This activity may include videos watched, posts liked, comments written, accounts followed, search history, and the amount of time spent on certain content. For example, if a student watches several videos about football, the system may record football as one of the student’s interests. If the student watches study tips, the system may also record learning content as a possible interest.

Following this, the data are analyzed by the algorithm. The system looks for patterns in the user’s behavior. It may compare one user’s activity with the activity of many other users. If many people who watch football videos also watch sports news, the system may decide that sports news is relevant content. This stage is important because the platform tries to predict what content will keep the user interested.

Subsequently, content is ranked by the recommendation system. Some videos are considered more suitable than others. Videos with high engagement, such as many likes, comments, shares, or long watch time, may be placed higher in the recommendation list. However, the recommendation is not based only on popularity. It is also affected by the user’s personal activity and the similarity between one video and another.

After that, selected videos are shown on the user’s feed. When the user watches, skips, likes, or comments on those videos, new data are created. This new data is then sent back to the system. As a result, the algorithm adjusts future recommendations. This process is called a feedback loop because the user’s response influences the next content that appears.

This system can be useful. It helps users find information, entertainment, tutorials, news, and learning materials more easily. A student can find English learning videos, science explanations, or scholarship information. However, the same system can also create problems if users are not careful. When similar videos are recommended repeatedly, users may spend too much time scrolling. This habit can reduce study time, sleep quality, and concentration.

Therefore, social media algorithms should be understood critically. They are not magic. They work by collecting data, analyzing patterns, ranking content, and showing recommendations. By understanding this process, students can become more responsible digital users. They can choose useful content, limit screen time, and use technology to support learning rather than distract from it.

Tasks
  1. Complete the flow: user activity is ___; data are ___; content is ___; selected videos are ___; user responses are sent back to the ___.
  2. Find five passive voice sentences.
  3. Find eight technical terms.
  4. Explain the feedback loop in your own words.
  5. Discuss: How can algorithms help and distract students?

Reading 3: How Transportation Costs Can Affect Prices on Remote Islands

Prices on remote islands can be affected by transportation costs. Many goods, such as rice, cooking oil, eggs, vegetables, fuel, and school supplies, are not always produced on small islands. They are often transported from the mainland or from larger islands by boat. Because of this, transportation becomes an important part of the distribution process.

Initially, goods are prepared by producers, suppliers, or traders in a larger market. The goods are packed and sent to a harbor. Following this, the goods are loaded onto a boat. The boat then carries the goods across the sea to the island. During normal weather, this process can run smoothly. However, when waves are high or the weather is unsafe, the boat schedule may be delayed.

When transportation is delayed, the supply of goods on the island may become limited. Shops may still have some stock, but the amount may not be enough for all consumers. If many people need the same goods while the stock is low, demand becomes higher than supply. As a result, prices may increase.

Transportation costs can also increase the final price of goods. Fuel, loading costs, labor, storage, and the risk of delay are included in the cost of distribution. When the cost of bringing goods to the island becomes higher, shop owners may need to sell the goods at a higher price. This does not always mean that sellers want to make excessive profit. Sometimes, prices rise because the cost of distribution has increased.

Subsequently, consumers may feel the impact. Families may need to spend more money on basic needs. Students may notice that snacks, books, or school materials become more expensive. If prices continue to rise while income stays the same, purchasing power decreases. This means people can buy fewer goods with the same amount of money.

Therefore, prices on remote islands are influenced by several connected factors. Supply, demand, weather, boat schedules, and transportation costs all play important roles. Understanding this process helps students see that economic changes are not random. They happen through a chain of causes and effects.

📜 Buka Listening ScriptKlik untuk membuka/menutup teks. Script disembunyikan agar siswa fokus menyimak terlebih dahulu.

Rainwater harvesting is a common way to collect and store water on small islands. This process is important because fresh water can be limited, especially during the dry season.

Initially, rain falls onto the roof of a house, school, or public building. The roof becomes the first surface that receives the water. Following this, the rainwater flows from the roof into gutters. The gutters are usually placed along the edge of the roof so the water can be directed to one place.

Next, the water is carried through pipes. These pipes connect the gutters to a tank, drum, or large container. In some houses, a simple filter is placed before the storage tank. The filter is used to reduce leaves, dust, or small dirt that may come from the roof.

Subsequently, the water is stored in a closed container. The container should be covered so mosquitoes, insects, and dirt cannot enter the water. If the water will be used for drinking, it should be boiled or treated first. This is important because rainwater may still contain small particles or germs.

Finally, the stored water can be used for daily needs such as washing, cleaning, watering plants, or cooking after proper treatment. As a result, families can have extra water when wells become salty or when fresh water is difficult to find.

In conclusion, rainwater harvesting works through several stages. Rain falls on the roof, water flows through gutters and pipes, dirt is reduced by a filter, and the water is stored safely. This process helps island communities manage water more carefully.

Writing Section

Gunakan panduan ini untuk menulis explanation text yang jelas, ilmiah, dan runtut.

How to Write an Explanation Text

  1. Choose a phenomenon or technology.
  2. Write a clear title.
  3. Write the general statement.
  4. List the stages.
  5. Add chronological connectors.
  6. Add passive voice.
  7. Add technical terms.
  8. Explain cause and effect.
  9. Write a closing statement.
  10. Revise for clarity.

Writing Template

Annotated Model Text: How Solar Panels Produce Electricity

Solar panels are devices that convert sunlight into electricity. They are useful in areas that receive strong sunlight, including many coastal and island communities.

Initially, sunlight is absorbed by the solar cells inside the panel. These solar cells are made from special materials that can react to sunlight. Following this, the energy from sunlight is converted into electrical energy. The electricity that is produced by the panel is usually direct current electricity.

Subsequently, the electricity is sent to an inverter. The inverter changes direct current into alternating current so it can be used by household devices. After that, the electricity can be used immediately or stored in a battery. When sunlight is not available, the stored electricity can be used at night or during cloudy weather.

In conclusion, solar panels work through a clear process. Sunlight is absorbed, energy is converted, electricity is changed by an inverter, and the power is used or stored. This technology can help communities use renewable energy more effectively.

PartExample
General StatementSolar panels are devices that convert sunlight into electricity.
ConnectorInitially, Following this, Subsequently, After that
Passive VoiceSunlight is absorbed; energy is converted; electricity is sent
Technical Termssolar panels, solar cells, electrical energy, direct current, inverter
ClosingIn conclusion, solar panels work through a clear process.

  2. Strong waves move sand away from the shore.
  3. Solar panels produce electricity.
  4. Boats transport goods to the island.

  2. The water ________ in a closed container.
  3. The signal ________ to the satellite.
  4. Similar videos ________ to users.

D. Error Correction

  1. Rainwater are collected in tanks.
  2. The signal is send to the satellite.
  3. Videos is recommended by the system.
  4. The coastline eroded by strong waves.
  5. Goods are transport by boat.

E. Mini Paragraph Practice

Write a short paragraph explaining one process. Use at least 4 sentences, 2 passive voice sentences, 3 chronological connectors, and 3 technical terms.

Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them

Wrong SentenceWhy It Is WrongCorrect SentenceArti Bahasa Indonesia
Rainwater are collected.Rainwater is uncountable, use “is”.Rainwater is collected.Air hujan dikumpulkan.
The signal is send.Use past participle “sent”.The signal is sent.Sinyal dikirim.
Videos is recommended.Plural subject uses “are”.Videos are recommended.Video direkomendasikan.
The coastline eroded by waves.Missing “is”.The coastline is eroded by waves.Garis pantai terkikis oleh ombak.
Goods are transport by boat.Use past participle “transported”.Goods are transported by boat.Barang diangkut dengan kapal.
Then then then the water flows.Too repetitive.Then, the water flows through pipes.Kemudian, air mengalir melalui pipa.
Algorithm make videos.Subject-verb error and unclear meaning.The algorithm recommends videos.Algoritma merekomendasikan video.
The rainwater collected in tank.Missing “is” and article.The rainwater is collected in a tank.Air hujan dikumpulkan di tandon.
This text tell how erosion.Incorrect verb and incomplete idea.This text explains how erosion happens.Teks ini menjelaskan bagaimana abrasi terjadi.
First, coastal erosion is dangerous.Not a process stage.First, waves hit the coastline.Pertama, ombak menghantam garis pantai.
The data is analyze.Wrong verb form.The data is analyzed.Data dianalisis.
The process because waves.Incomplete cause-effect structure.The process happens because waves hit the shore repeatedly.Proses terjadi karena ombak menghantam pantai berulang kali.
Finally, the first stage begins.Illogical sequence.Initially, the first stage begins.Pada awalnya, tahap pertama dimulai.
The system is recommend videos.Wrong passive form.Videos are recommended by the system.Video direkomendasikan oleh sistem.
Internet satellite work by signal.Grammar and word order problem.Satellite internet works by transmitting signals through satellites.Internet satelit bekerja dengan mengirimkan sinyal melalui satelit.

Final Project

Buat infografis ilmiah atau presentasi PowerPoint kelompok yang menerangkan alur kerja teknologi modern atau fenomena ilmiah/sosial.

Scientific Infographic or Group PowerPoint

Product Options: one-page scientific infographic or PowerPoint presentation with 6–8 slides.

Topic Choices: satellite internet, social media algorithms, solar panels, rainwater harvesting, coastal erosion, tidal floods, plastic waste, online learning platforms, transportation costs, or seaweed farming.

Product Requirements

  • One clear title.
  • One general statement.
  • At least five process stages.
  • At least eight technical terms.
  • At least six chronological connectors.
  • At least five passive voice sentences.
  • A cause-effect explanation.
  • A clear visual flow.
  • A conclusion.
  • Information sources.

Suggested PowerPoint Structure

SlideContent
Slide 1Title, group members, topic
Slide 2General statement and why the topic matters
Slide 3Key technical terms
Slide 4Process stages 1–2
Slide 5Process stages 3–5
Slide 6Cause-effect explanation
Slide 7Impact on island life
Slide 8Conclusion and sources

Group Roles

RoleResponsibility
ResearcherFinds accurate information
WriterWrites explanation sentences
Language CheckerChecks passive voice, connectors, and vocabulary
DesignerDesigns infographic or slides
PresenterPresents the project
Time KeeperHelps the group finish on time

Presentation Script Template

Good morning, everyone. Our group will explain [topic].

This process is important because [reason].

Initially, [stage 1]. Following this, [stage 2]. Subsequently, [stage 3]. After that, [stage 4]. Finally, [stage 5].

This process is affected by [factor]. As a result, [effect].

In conclusion, [summary]. Thank you.

Reflection, Enrichment, and Remedial

Gunakan bagian ini untuk menilai perkembangan diri dan memilih latihan lanjutan.

Self-Reflection Questions

  1. What process can I explain better now?
  2. Which technical terms did I learn?
  3. How can passive voice make my explanation sound more scientific?
  4. What local phenomenon around me can be explained scientifically?
  5. How can I use English to explain technology or nature?

Learning Scale

1 = I need more practice. 2 = I understand some parts. 3 = I can explain with help. 4 = I can explain independently. 5 = I can explain and teach others.

Enrichment Tasks

  • Compare two explanation texts from different fields: technology and environment.
  • Create a bilingual infographic in English and Indonesian.
  • Record a 3-minute explanation video.
  • Research a local environmental issue and explain the process scientifically.
  • Add data or simple statistics to your explanation.

Remedial Tasks

  • Complete missing connectors in a paragraph.
  • Match technical terms with meanings.
  • Change five active sentences into passive voice.
  • Arrange scrambled explanation stages.
  • Write a short explanation using a paragraph frame.
